sentences.zh: 孔靖

translations.literal: Kong Jing
translations.idiomatic: Kong Jing

sentences.zh: 孔靖字季恭，會稽山陰人也。

translations.literal: Kong Jing, courtesy name Jigong, was a native of Shanyin in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Jing, styled Jigong, came from Shanyin in Kuaiji commandery.

sentences.zh: 名與高祖祖諱同，故稱字。

translations.literal: His given name was identical to the taboo name of Gaozu's grandfather, so he was known by his courtesy name.
translations.idiomatic: Because his personal name matched the ancestral taboo of the High Founder's grandfather, he was addressed by his style rather than his given name.

sentences.zh: 祖愉，晉車騎將軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yu was Jin Chariot-and-Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yu served the Jin as Chariot-and-Cavalry General.

sentences.zh: 父誾，散騎常侍。

translations.literal: His father Yin was Attendant at the Chamberlain for Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yin held the post of attendant at the chamberlain for attendants.

sentences.zh: 季恭始察郡孝廉，功曹史，著作佐郎，太子舍人，鎮軍司馬，司徒左西掾。

translations.literal: Jigong at first was nominated Filial and Incorrupt by the inspectorate, then served as clerical officer, assistant gentleman of the Secretariat, attendant in the heir apparent's household, army marshal of the Pacification Army, and western clerk on the left of the Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: Jigong began as a commandery nominee for filial conduct and incorruptibility, then rose through posts as clerical officer, assistant gentleman in the Secretariat, attendant in the crown prince's household, marshal of the Pacification Army, and western clerk under the minister over the masses.

sentences.zh: 未拜，遭母憂。

translations.literal: Before he could take up appointment, he suffered his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: Before he assumed office, his mother died and he entered mourning.

sentences.zh: 隆安五年，於喪中被起建威將軍、山陰令，不就。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Long'an, while still in mourning he was summoned to be General Who Establishes Might and magistrate of Shanyin, but he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In Long'an year 5, even during mourning he was called up as General Who Establishes Might and magistrate of Shanyin, but he declined.

sentences.zh: 高祖東征孫恩，屢至會稽，季恭曲意禮接，贍給甚厚。

translations.literal: When Gaozu campaigned east against Sun En, he repeatedly came to Kuaiji; Jigong received him with elaborate courtesy and supplied him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu marched east against Sun En, he often passed through Kuaiji; Jigong went out of his way to honor him and provisioned his forces lavishly.

sentences.zh: 高祖後討孫恩，時桓玄篡形已著，欲於山陰建義討之。

translations.literal: Later, when Gaozu again campaigned against Sun En, Huan Xuan's usurpation was already evident, and Gaozu wished to raise arms at Shanyin to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: On a later campaign against Sun En, Huan Xuan's plot to seize the throne was already plain, and Gaozu meant to launch a righteous rising from Shanyin to overthrow him.

sentences.zh: 季恭以為山陰去京邑路遠，且玄未居極位，不如待其篡逆事彰，釁成惡稔，徐於京口圖之，不憂不剋。

translations.literal: Jigong held that Shanyin was far from the capital by road, and that since Xuan had not yet reached the supreme position, it would be better to wait until his usurpation stood fully revealed, his guilt ripened, and then plot slowly from Jingkou—there would be no worry of failure.
translations.idiomatic: Jigong argued that Shanyin lay too far from the capital, and that since Xuan had not yet taken the throne outright, they should wait until his treason was unmistakable and his crimes fully ripe, then strike gradually from Jingkou—success would be assured.

sentences.zh: 高祖亦謂為然。

translations.literal: Gaozu also considered this correct.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu agreed.

sentences.zh: 虞嘯父為征東將軍、會稽內史，季恭初求為府司馬，不得。

translations.literal: Yu Xiaofu was General Who Pacifies the East and interior administrator of Kuaiji; Jigong at first sought to be his headquarters marshal but did not obtain the post.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xiaofu held the posts of General Who Pacifies the East and interior administrator of Kuaiji; Jigong had earlier sought a marshal's appointment on his staff but was refused.

sentences.zh: 及帝定桓玄，以季恭為內史，使齎封板拜授，正與季恭相值，季恭便回舟夜還。

translations.literal: When the emperor had settled Huan Xuan, he appointed Jigong interior administrator and sent someone bearing the sealed commission to invest him; they happened to meet Jigong on the way, and Jigong at once turned his boat and returned by night.
translations.idiomatic: After the throne had suppressed Huan Xuan, Jigong was named interior administrator and an envoy was sent with the sealed patent of appointment; he met the envoy on the road, turned his boat about, and reached home that same night.

sentences.zh: 至即叩扉告嘯父，并令掃拂別齋，即便入郡。

translations.literal: On arrival he knocked at the door to inform Xiaofu, and also ordered a separate lodging swept and prepared, then at once entered the commandery seat.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as he arrived he knocked at Xiaofu's door to announce himself, had a side chamber cleaned for his use, and entered the administrative city without delay.

sentences.zh: 嘯父本為桓玄所授，聞玄敗，震懼，開門請罪。

translations.literal: Xiaofu had originally been appointed by Huan Xuan; hearing of Xuan's defeat, he was shaken with fear and opened his gate to plead guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaofu had owed his appointment to Huan Xuan; when he heard of Xuan's fall he was terrified and came out to submit and beg pardon.

sentences.zh: 季恭慰勉，使且安所住，明旦乃移。

translations.literal: Jigong comforted and encouraged him, telling him to remain for the time being where he was lodging and to move only the next morning.
translations.idiomatic: Jigong reassured him and told him to stay where he was until the next day before moving out.

sentences.zh: 季恭到任，務存治實，敕止浮華，翦罰遊惰，由是寇盜衰止，境內肅清。

translations.literal: When Jigong took office, he devoted himself to solid governance, forbade empty display, and cut down idlers and the indolent; thereby banditry declined and ceased, and within the borders all was orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office Jigong pursued practical administration, curbed ostentation, and punished loafers and the idle; banditry dwindled away and the commandery grew calm and clean.

sentences.zh: 徵為右衞將軍，加給事中，不拜。

translations.literal: He was summoned as General of the Right Guard, with additional appointment as Supervising Attendant, but he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was called up as General of the Right Guard with an additional post as supervising attendant, but declined.

sentences.zh: 尋除侍中，領本國中正，徙琅邪王大司馬司馬。

translations.literal: Soon he was removed to be Palace Attendant, heading the chief rectifier of his native commandery, then transferred as army marshal to the Prince of Langye, Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made palace attendant and chief rectifier of his home commandery, then transferred to serve as army marshal on the staff of the Prince of Langye, grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 尋出為吳興太守，加冠軍。

translations.literal: Soon he went out as governor of Wuxing, with additional title Champion.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was sent out as governor of Wuxing with the additional rank of champion general.

sentences.zh: 先是，吳興頻喪太守，云項羽神為卞山王，居郡聽事，二千石至，常避之，季恭居聽事，竟無害也。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wuxing had repeatedly lost its governors; it was said that the spirit of Xiang Yu as King of Mount Bian dwelt in the commandery audience hall, and when a two-thousand-bushel official arrived he always avoided it—yet Jigong occupied the hall and suffered no harm.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, Wuxing had lost one governor after another; people said the god of Xiang Yu, as King of Mount Bian, haunted the commandery hall and that incoming governors always steered clear—yet Jigong took up residence there and came to no harm.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書右僕射，固讓。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing but firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right vice director of the Masters of Writing but firmly declined the post.

sentences.zh: 義熙八年，復督五郡諸軍、征虜、會稽內史。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yixi he again supervised the armies of five commanderies as General Who Captures Barbarians and interior administrator of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: In Yixi year 8 he again took command of the armies of five commanderies as General Who Captures Barbarians and interior administrator of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 修飾學校，督課誦習。

translations.literal: He refurbished the schools and supervised lessons in recitation and study.
translations.idiomatic: He restored the schools and supervised students in their recitation and study.

sentences.zh: 十年，復為尚書右僕射，加散騎常侍，又讓不拜。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was again made Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, with additional Attendant at the Chamberlain for Attendants, and again declined without accepting.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10 he was again named right vice director of the Masters of Writing with an additional post as attendant at the chamberlain for attendants, and once more declined.

sentences.zh: 頃之，除領軍將軍，加散騎常侍，本州大中正。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed General of the Palace Guard, with additional Attendant at the Chamberlain for Attendants and grand rectifier of his home province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made General of the Palace Guard, with additional rank as attendant at the chamberlain for attendants and as grand rectifier of his native province.

sentences.zh: 十二年，致仕，拜金紫光錄大夫，常侍如故。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he retired from office and was granted the golden seal and purple ribbon as Recorder Grandee, his attendant post remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12 he retired and was honored as recorder grandee with the golden seal and purple ribbon, while retaining his attendant title.

sentences.zh: 是歲，高祖北伐，季恭求從，以為太尉軍諮祭酒、後將軍。

translations.literal: That year, when Gaozu campaigned north, Jigong asked to accompany him and was appointed staff adviser and libationer of the Grand Marshal's army and Rear General.
translations.idiomatic: That year Gaozu marched north; Jigong asked to go with the expedition and was named staff adviser and libationer on the grand marshal's army staff and rear general.

sentences.zh: 從平關、洛。

translations.literal: He followed in the pacification of Guan and Luo.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the conquest of the passes and Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 高祖為相國，又隨府遷。

translations.literal: When Gaozu became Chancellor of State, Jigong again followed the headquarters in its transfer.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu became chancellor of state, Jigong moved with his staff once more.

sentences.zh: 宋臺初建，令書以為尚書令，加散騎常侍，又讓不受，乃拜侍中、特進、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When the Song administration was first established, an order appointed him Director of the Masters of Writing with additional Attendant at the Chamberlain for Attendants; he again declined and did not accept, and was then invested as Palace Attendant, Special Advance, and Left Household Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song regime was first set up, he was ordered to become director of the Masters of Writing with an additional post as attendant at the chamberlain for attendants; he declined again, and was then appointed palace attendant, special advance, and left household grandee.

sentences.zh: 辭事東歸，高祖餞之戲馬臺，百僚咸賦詩以述其美。

translations.literal: He resigned his duties and returned east; Gaozu gave him a farewell feast at Terrace of the Sportive Horse, and the hundred officials all composed poems to praise his excellence.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned and went home to the east; Gaozu feasted him at the Terrace of the Sportive Horse, and the whole bureaucracy wrote poems in praise of him.

sentences.zh: 及受命，加開府儀同三司，辭讓累年，終以不受。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the Mandate, Jigong was given the equivalence of the Three Dukes with an open office, but he declined year after year and in the end never accepted.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu took the throne, he was offered open office with ritual parity to the three dukes; Jigong declined for years and never accepted.

sentences.zh: 永初三年，薨，時年七十六。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongchu he died, aged seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yongchu year 3, at the age of seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 追贈侍中、左光祿大夫、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted Palace Attendant, Left Household Grandee, and open office with ritual parity to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as palace attendant, left household grandee, and holder of open office with parity to the three dukes.
