sentences.zh: 子 山士

translations.literal: Son: Shanshi
translations.idiomatic: Son: Shanshi

sentences.zh: =子山士，歷顯位，侍中，會稽太守，坐小弟駕部郎道穰逼略良家子女，白衣領郡。

translations.literal: His son Shanshi held prominent posts, including Palace Attendant and governor of Kuaiji; because his younger brother, Secretariat Master of Carriages Daorang, had coerced daughters of good families, he served the commandery in plain dress.
translations.idiomatic: Shanshi rose to high office, including palace attendant and governor of Kuaiji; when his younger brother Daorang of the directorate of carriages forced himself on daughters of respectable families, Shanshi was reduced to serving the commandery in undress.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十七年，卒官。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in Yuanjia year 27.

translations.literal: Section divider in the source text.

sentences.zh: 子 靈符

translations.literal: Son: Lingfu
translations.idiomatic: Son: Lingfu

sentences.zh: =弟靈符，元嘉末，為南譙王義宣司空長史、南郡太守，尚書吏部郎。

translations.literal: His younger brother Lingfu, at the end of Yuanjia, was chief clerk to the Minister of Works for the Prince of Nanqiao, Yixuan, governor of Nan commandery, and Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Lingfu, late in Yuanjia, served the Prince of Nanqiao Yixuan as chief clerk to the minister of works and governor of Nan commandery, and as a gentleman in the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 世祖大明初，自侍中為輔國將軍、郢州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daming under Shizu, he moved from Palace Attendant to General Who Assists the State and inspector of Ying province.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Daming era under Emperor Xiaowu, he left the palace attendant post to become General Who Assists the State and inspector of Ying province.

sentences.zh: 入為丹陽尹。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Intendant of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was brought in as intendant of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 山陰縣土境褊狹，民多田少，靈符表徙無貲之家於餘姚、鄞、鄮三縣界，墾起湖田。

translations.literal: Shanyin county's territory was narrow and cramped, with many people and little land; Lingfu memorialized to move households without means to the borders of Yuyao, Yin, and Mao counties and to open lake fields for cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: Shanyin county was cramped for land and its people had too little farmland; Lingfu proposed relocating impoverished households to the margins of Yuyao, Yin, and Mao counties and reclaiming lake bottom for fields.

sentences.zh: 上使公卿博議，太宰江夏王義恭議曰：「夫訓農修本，有國所同，土著之民，習翫日久，如京師無田，不聞徙居他縣。

translations.literal: The emperor had the ministers debate broadly. The Grand Mentor, Prince of Jiangxia Yigong, argued: "To instruct in agriculture and restore the root is what every state shares; native inhabitants have long grown accustomed to their ways—as in the capital, where those without fields are not heard of as moving to other counties."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered a full debate among the chief ministers. The grand mentor, Prince of Jiangxia Yigong, argued: "Teaching agriculture and strengthening the rural foundation is common to every state; people rooted in their native soil have long settled habits—even in the capital, one never hears of the landless being moved to other counties."

sentences.zh: 尋山陰豪族富室，頃畝不少，貧者肆力，非為無處，耕起空荒，無救災歉。

translations.literal: "Moreover, among Shanyin's powerful clans and wealthy houses, not a few hold ample acreage; the poor can exert their strength—there is not truly no place for them. Opening empty wasteland will not remedy famine years."
translations.idiomatic: "Besides, Shanyin's great families already hold plenty of land; the poor can still find work—it is not that they have nowhere to turn. Reclaiming empty ground will not cure years of disaster and shortage."

sentences.zh: 又緣湖居民，魚鴨為業，及有居肆，理無樂徙。

translations.literal: "Again, lakeside dwellers make fish and ducks their livelihood, and some keep shops—by reason they cannot be glad to move."
translations.idiomatic: "And those who live along the lakes earn their living from fish and fowl, or run shops—they cannot reasonably be expected to welcome relocation."

sentences.zh: 」尚書令柳元景、右僕射劉秀之、尚書王瓚之、顧凱之、顏師伯、嗣湘東王彧議曰：「富戶溫房，無假遷業；

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Liu Yuanjing, Right Vice Director Liu Xiuzhi, Masters of Writing Wang Zanzhi, Gu Kaizhi, Yan Shibo, and the heir Prince of Xiangdong Yu argued: "Wealthy households in warm houses have no need to change their occupation;"
translations.idiomatic: Director Liu Yuanjing, right vice director Liu Xiuzhi, masters of writing Wang Zanzhi, Gu Kaizhi, Yan Shibo, and the heir Prince of Xiangdong Yu argued: "Rich households in comfortable homes have no reason to change trades;"

sentences.zh: 窮身寒室，必應徙居。

translations.literal: "those in poverty in cold chambers must be moved."
translations.idiomatic: "but the destitute in cold hovels ought to be relocated."

sentences.zh: 葺宇疏臯，產粒無待，資公則公未易充，課私則私卒難具。

translations.literal: "With patched roofs and sparse marshland, grain cannot be awaited; if the public treasury is relied on, it is not easily filled, and if private households are taxed, they can hardly be made complete."
translations.idiomatic: "With patched roofs over marginal land, harvests cannot be counted on; public funds will not easily suffice, and private households cannot quickly be made whole."

sentences.zh: 生計既完，畬功自息，宜募亡叛通卹及與樂田者，其往經創，須粗修立，然後徙居。

translations.literal: "Once livelihoods are secured, the work of clearing fields will cease of itself. It is fitting to recruit fugitives, absconders, and those willing to farm; where they go has suffered devastation and must first be roughly restored, and only then should people be moved."
translations.idiomatic: "Once livelihoods are secure, reclamation will take care of itself. Recruit fugitives, absconders, and men willing to till the soil; the lands they are sent to have been ravaged and must be roughly put in order before anyone is moved there."

sentences.zh: 」侍中沈懷文、王景文、黃門侍郎劉敳、郄顒議曰：「百姓雖不親農，不無資生之路，若驅以就田，則坐相違奪。

translations.literal: Palace Attendants Shen Huaiwen and Wang Jingwen, and Yellow Gate Attendants Liu Kan and Xi Yan argued: "Though the common people do not personally farm, they are not without means to live; if they are driven to the fields, they will simply be robbed of their livelihoods."
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendants Shen Huaiwen and Wang Jingwen and yellow gate attendants Liu Kan and Xi Yan argued: "Even when the people do not farm themselves, they still have ways to live; drive them onto the land and you simply strip them of their livelihood."

sentences.zh: 且鄞等三縣，去治並遠，既安之民，忽徙他邑，新垣未立，舊居已毀，去留兩困，無以自資。

translations.literal: "Moreover, Yin and the other three counties are all far from the seat of government; people already settled are suddenly moved to other districts—new walls are not yet built while old dwellings are already destroyed; whether they go or stay, both ways bring hardship, and they have no means to support themselves."
translations.idiomatic: "Yin and the other counties lie far from the prefectural seat; people long settled are suddenly uprooted—new homes are not yet built while old ones are already lost; whether they go or stay they are trapped, with no way to support themselves."

sentences.zh: 謂宜適任民情，從其所樂，開宥逋亡，且令就業，若審成腴壤，然後議遷。

translations.literal: "We hold that one should suit the people's feelings, follow what they delight in, grant amnesty to fugitives, and for the present let them take up work; if it is verified that fertile soil has been created, then afterward discuss relocation."
translations.idiomatic: "We say policy should fit the people's wishes and let them do what they prefer: pardon fugitives and let them find work for now; only after the new land is truly fertile should relocation be debated."

sentences.zh: 」太常王玄謨議曰：「小民貧匱，遠就荒疇，去舊即新，糧種俱闕，習之既難，勸之未易。

translations.literal: Minister of Ceremonies Wang Xuanmo argued: "Small folk are poor and destitute; to go far into waste fields, leave the old and take up the new—grain and seed are both lacking; habit is already hard, and exhortation is not easy."
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Ceremonies Wang Xuanmo argued: "Common people are poor; send them far into wasteland, tear them from the old and thrust them into the new—food and seed are both lacking; the habit is hard to form and persuasion is not easy."

sentences.zh: 謂宜微加資給，使得肆勤，明力田之賞，申怠惰之罰。

translations.literal: "We hold that a modest subsidy should be added so that they may exert themselves freely, with clear rewards for those who work the fields and penalties declared for the idle."
translations.idiomatic: "Give them modest support so they can labor freely, make rewards for diligent farming clear, and enforce penalties on the lazy."

sentences.zh: 」光祿勳王昇之議曰：「遠廢之疇，方翦荊棘，率課窮乏，其事彌難，資徙粗立，徐行無晚。

translations.literal: Household Grandee Wang Sheng argued: "In distant abandoned fields the brambles have only just been cut; to lead and tax the destitute makes the task all the harder. Let support for the migrants be roughly established first; to proceed slowly is not too late."
translations.idiomatic: Household grandee Wang Sheng argued: "Distant abandoned fields are only now being cleared of thorns; pressing the poor into service makes the task harder still. Establish support for the migrants first; there is no harm in moving slowly."

sentences.zh: 」上違議，從其徙民，並成良業。

translations.literal: The emperor went against the various opinions and followed Lingfu's plan to move the people; all came to prosper in their new occupations.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rejected the opposing views, adopted Lingfu's relocation plan, and the migrants all established successful livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 靈符自丹陽出為會稽太守，尋加豫章王子尚撫軍長史。

translations.literal: Lingfu left Danyang to become governor of Kuaiji, and soon was additionally made chief clerk to the Pacification Army of the Prince of Yuzhang, Zishang.
translations.idiomatic: Lingfu left the capital post to become governor of Kuaiji and was soon also named chief clerk on the pacification army staff of the Prince of Yuzhang, Zishang.

sentences.zh: 靈符家本豐，產業甚廣，又於永興立墅，周回三十三里，水陸地二百六十五頃，含帶二山，又有果園九處。

translations.literal: Lingfu's family was originally wealthy, with very extensive holdings; he also established a manor at Yongxing, thirty-three li in circuit, with two hundred sixty-five qing of land by water and on land, embracing two mountains, and nine orchards besides.
translations.idiomatic: Lingfu's family was already rich with vast estates; he also built a manor at Yongxing thirty-three li around, holding 265 qing of land and water, including two hills and nine orchards.

sentences.zh: 為有司所糾，詔原之，而靈符答對不實，坐以免官。

translations.literal: He was impeached by the relevant offices; an edict pardoned him, but because Lingfu's replies were untrue, he was punished by removal from office.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities impeached him; an edict pardoned the offense, but because Lingfu's answers were false he was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 後復舊官，又為尋陽王子房右軍長史，太守如故。

translations.literal: Later he recovered his former posts and was again chief clerk of the Right Army for the Prince of Xunyang, Zifang, while retaining the governorship.
translations.idiomatic: He later regained his offices and also served as chief clerk of the right army for the Prince of Xunyang, Zifang, while keeping the governorship.

sentences.zh: 慤實有材幹，不存華飾，每所蒞官，政績修理。

translations.literal: Sincere and solid, he possessed ability; he did not keep up empty display, and in every office he held his administrative achievements were well ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Earnest and capable, he shunned ostentation; wherever he served, his administration was sound and orderly.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝景和中，犯忤近臣，為所讒搆，遣鞭殺之。

translations.literal: Under the Deposed Emperor, in the Jinghe era, he offended a favorite minister and was slandered and framed by him; he was sent orders to be flogged to death.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jinghe era under the Deposed Emperor he offended a court favorite, was framed by him, and was ordered beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 二子湛之、淵之，於都賜死。

translations.literal: His two sons Zhanzhi and Yuanzhi were granted death in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: His two sons Zhanzhi and Yuanzhi were ordered to take their own lives in the capital.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，追贈靈符金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, Lingfu was posthumously granted Household Grandee with the golden seal and purple ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xiaowen came to the throne, Lingfu was posthumously honored as household grandee with the golden seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 淵之大明中為尚書比部郎。

translations.literal: Yuanzhi, in the Daming era, was Gentleman of the Comparative Section in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhi served in the Daming era as a gentleman in the comparative section of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 時安陸應城縣民張江陵與妻吳共罵母黃令死，黃忿恨自經死，值赦。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Jiangling of Yingcheng county in Anlu, together with his wife Wu, reviled his mother Huang until she wished to die; Huang, in resentful rage, hanged herself. There happened to be an amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhang Jiangling of Yingcheng in Anlu and his wife Wu together abused his mother Huang until she wished for death; in fury she hanged herself. An amnesty was in effect.

sentences.zh: 律文，子賊殺傷毆父母，梟首，罵詈，棄市，謀殺夫之父母，亦棄市。

translations.literal: The statutes provide: a child who as a villain kills, wounds, or beats parents is decapitated and the head displayed; reviling and cursing is execution in the marketplace; plotting to kill a husband's parents is also execution in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: The code states that a child who kills, injures, or beats parents is beheaded and the head exposed; cursing and reviling is punished by execution in the market; plotting to kill a husband's parents is likewise market execution.

sentences.zh: 值赦，免刑補冶。

translations.literal: When an amnesty occurred, punishment was remitted and the offender was assigned to the ironworks.
translations.idiomatic: Under amnesty the death penalty was commuted to service in the state ironworks.

sentences.zh: 江陵罵母，母以之自裁，重於傷毆。

translations.literal: Jiangling reviled his mother, and his mother took her own life because of it—this is heavier than wounding or beating.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangling cursed his mother until she killed herself—a graver wrong than mere injury or beating.

sentences.zh: 若同殺科，則疑重，用毆傷及罵科，則疑輕。

translations.literal: If treated under the statute for killing, it seems perhaps too severe; if the statutes for beating and wounding or for reviling are applied, it seems perhaps too light.
translations.idiomatic: To apply the homicide statute might be too harsh; to apply the statutes on beating or cursing might be too lenient.

sentences.zh: 制唯有打母，遇赦猶梟首，無罵母致死值赦之科。

translations.literal: The regulations have only the case of beating one's mother, where even under amnesty the head is still displayed; there is no statute for reviling one's mother to death when an amnesty applies.
translations.idiomatic: The code explicitly covers beating one's mother—even under amnesty the head is still exposed—but has no provision for cursing one's mother to death under amnesty.

sentences.zh: 淵之議曰：「夫題里逆心，而仁者不入，名且惡之，況乃人事。

translations.literal: Yuanzhi argued: "When a village posts a man's name for a rebellious heart, the humane do not enter; even the name is detested—how much more so in human affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhi argued: "When a village posts a man's name for treachery, the humane will not enter his door; even the name is loathed—how much more so when it comes to human conduct."

sentences.zh: 故毆傷呪詛，法所不原，詈之致盡，則理無可宥。

translations.literal: Therefore beating, wounding, and cursing are what the law does not pardon; when reviling drives one to the end, by principle there is no forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: Beating, injury, and cursing are never pardoned by law; when cursing drives a parent to death, reason offers no excuse.

sentences.zh: 罰有從輕，蓋疑失善，求之文旨，非此之謂。

translations.literal: That punishments may follow the lighter measure is because doubt favors the good; sought in the text's intent, this case is not of that kind.
translations.idiomatic: Leniency in punishment reflects doubt in favor of the accused; read against the spirit of the code, this case does not qualify.

sentences.zh: 江陵雖值赦恩，故合梟首。

translations.literal: Though Jiangling encountered an amnesty, he should therefore be decapitated and his head displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Even with the amnesty, Jiangling should still be beheaded and his head exposed.

sentences.zh: 婦本以義，愛非天屬，黃之所恨，情不在吳，原死補冶，有允正法。

translations.literal: A wife is bound by righteousness, not by natural kinship; Huang's resentment was not directed at Wu. To remit death and assign to the ironworks accords with proper law.
translations.idiomatic: A daughter-in-law is tied by duty, not by blood; Huang's grievance was not aimed at Wu. Commuting her death to service in the ironworks fits the law.

sentences.zh: 」詔如淵之議，吳免棄市。

translations.literal: An edict followed Yuanzhi's opinion; Wu was spared execution in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved Yuanzhi's opinion; Wu was spared market execution.

sentences.zh: 羊玄保

translations.literal: Yang Xuanbao
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xuanbao

sentences.zh: 羊玄保，太山南城人也。

translations.literal: Yang Xuanbao was a native of Nancheng in Taishan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xuanbao came from Nancheng in Taishan commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖楷，尚書都官郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Kai was Gentleman of the Masters of Writing for the Capital Offices.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Kai was a gentleman in the capital offices section of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 父綏，中書侍郎。

translations.literal: His father Sui was Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sui was attendant gentleman of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 玄保起家楚臺太常博士，遭母憂，服闕，右將軍何無忌、前將軍諸葛長民俱板為參軍，並不就。

translations.literal: Xuanbao began his career as a Erudite of the Chamberlain for Ceremonials on the Chu administration staff; he suffered his mother's death, and when mourning ended, both General of the Right He Wuji and General of the Van Zhuge Changmin summoned him as staff officer, but he accepted neither.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanbao began as an erudite of the chamberlain for ceremonials on the Chu regime staff; after his mother's death and the end of mourning, Generals He Wuji and Zhuge Changmin both offered him staff posts, but he declined both.

sentences.zh: 除臨安令。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Lin'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 劉穆之舉為高祖鎮軍參軍，庫部郎，永世令。

translations.literal: Liu Muzhi recommended him as staff officer to Gaozu's Pacification Army, Gentleman of the Storehouse Section, and magistrate of Yongshi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Muzhi recommended him as a staff officer on Gaozu's pacification army, as gentleman of the storehouse section, and as magistrate of Yongshi.

sentences.zh: 復為高祖太尉參軍，轉主簿，丹陽丞。

translations.literal: He again served as staff officer to Gaozu as Grand Marshal, then was transferred to chief clerk and assistant intendant of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: He again served on Gaozu's grand marshal staff, then became chief clerk and assistant intendant of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 少帝景平二年，入為尚書右丞，轉左丞，司徒右長史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingping under the Lesser Emperor he entered the Masters of Writing as Right Assistant Director, then Left Assistant Director, and Chief Clerk on the Right of the Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingping year 2 under Emperor Shao he entered the Masters of Writing as right assistant director, then left assistant director, and chief clerk on the right under the minister over the masses.

sentences.zh: 府公王弘甚知重之，謂左長史庾登之、吏部尚書王准之曰：「卿二賢明美朗識，會悟多通，然弘懿之望，故當共推羊也。

translations.literal: The lord of the headquarters, Wang Hong, valued him highly and said to Chief Clerk on the Left Yu Dengzhi and Minister of Personnel Wang Zhunzhi: "You two are worthy, bright in understanding, quick to grasp and broadly versed, yet in breadth and depth of virtue it is Yang who should be jointly advanced."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong, head of the office, thought highly of him and told chief clerk Yu Dengzhi and minister of personnel Wang Zhunzhi: "You are both able and quick-witted, but in breadth and steadiness of character we should together advance Yang."

sentences.zh: 」頃之，入為黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Before long he entered the palace as Yellow Gate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was brought in as yellow gate attendant.

sentences.zh: 善弈棊，棊品第三，太祖與賭郡戲，勝，以補宣城太守。

translations.literal: He was skilled at weiqi, ranked third in playing strength; Taizu wagered a commandery in a game with him, and when Xuanbao won, he was appointed to fill the post of governor of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at go and ranked third in the realm; Taizu wagered a commandery in a match, and when Xuanbao won he was appointed governor of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 先是，劉式之為宣城，立吏民亡叛制，一人不禽，符伍里吏送州作部，若獲者賞位二階。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Liu Shizhi was governor of Xuancheng, he established a regulation on officials and people who fled or rebelled: if one person was not captured, the order went to the five-household unit and the village clerk to send him to the province as corvée labor; if captured, the reward was advancement two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Liu Shizhi governed Xuancheng, he instituted rules on fugitives and rebels: if even one was not caught, the local group and village clerk had to send a substitute to provincial labor; capture brought a two-rank reward.

sentences.zh: 玄保以為非宜，陳之曰：「臣伏尋亡叛之由，皆出於窮逼，未有足以推存而樂為此者也。

translations.literal: Xuanbao considered this unsuitable and stated: "Your servant respectfully reflects that the causes of flight and rebellion all arise from desperate hardship; there has never been anyone with enough to live on who delighted in doing this."
translations.idiomatic: Xuanbao judged this unwise and memorialized: "I have considered the causes of flight and rebellion: they all spring from desperate poverty; no one with a decent livelihood chooses such a course."

sentences.zh: 今立殊制，於事為苦。

translations.literal: "Now to establish an exceptional regulation makes the matter bitter in practice."
translations.idiomatic: "To impose a special rule now only adds hardship."

sentences.zh: 臣聞苦節不可貞，懼致流弊。

translations.literal: "Your servant has heard that harsh discipline cannot long endure; I fear it will lead to spreading abuses."
translations.idiomatic: "I have heard that harsh measures cannot hold; I fear they will breed further abuses."

sentences.zh: 昔龔遂譬民於亂繩，緩之然後可理，黃覇以寬和為用，不以嚴刻為先。

translations.literal: "In the past Gong Sui likened the people to tangled rope—only when loosened could they be put in order; Huang Ba took leniency and harmony as his tools and did not put severity first."
translations.idiomatic: "Gong Sui compared the people to tangled rope—only when loosened could it be straightened; Huang Ba governed through leniency and harmony rather than severity."

sentences.zh: 臣愚以謂單身逃役，便為盡戶。

translations.literal: "Your servant foolishly holds that when a single person flees corvée, the whole household is treated as guilty."
translations.idiomatic: "I believe that when one man flees labor service, the whole household is punished."

sentences.zh: 今一人不測，坐者甚多，既憚重負，各為身計，牽挽逃竄，必致繁滋。

translations.literal: "Now when one person absconds without warning, many are implicated; fearing heavy burdens, each schemes for himself, dragging others into flight—this will surely breed ever greater trouble."
translations.idiomatic: "When one man vanishes without warning, many are punished; fearing the burden, everyone looks out for himself and drags others into flight—the abuses will only multiply."

sentences.zh: 又能禽獲叛身，類非謹惜，既無堪能，坐陵勞吏，名器虛假，所妨實多，將階級不足供賞，服勤無以自勸。

translations.literal: "Moreover, those who can capture fugitives are generally not men who cherish caution; lacking real ability, they lord it over toiling clerks. Titles and rewards are hollow, the harm is great in fact, ranks will not suffice for rewards, and diligent service has no way to encourage itself."
translations.idiomatic: "Those who catch fugitives are rarely conscientious men; lacking real talent, they bully the clerks. Honors become empty, the harm is real, ranks will not cover the rewards promised, and honest effort wins no encouragement."

sentences.zh: 又尋此制，施一邦而已，若其是邪，則應與天下為一，若其非邪，亦不宜獨行一郡。

translations.literal: "Again, this regulation applies to only one commandery; if it is right, it should be unified with the empire, and if it is wrong, it should not be enforced alone in a single prefecture."
translations.idiomatic: "This rule applies to only one commandery; if it is sound, it should bind the whole realm; if it is unsound, it should not run alone in one prefecture."

sentences.zh: 民離憂患，其弊將甚。

translations.literal: "The people, torn from their cares, will suffer abuses all the more."
translations.idiomatic: "The people, driven from their livelihoods, will suffer all the more."

sentences.zh: 臣忝守所職，懼難遵用，致率管穴，冒以陳聞。

translations.literal: "Your servant, holding office in disgrace, fears difficulty in following and applying it, and therefore leads the narrow view of a mole's burrow in daring to report this."
translations.idiomatic: "Your servant holds his post in shame, fears he cannot enforce this rule, and ventures this humble report from his limited view."

sentences.zh: 」由此此制得停。

translations.literal: Because of this, the regulation was halted.
translations.idiomatic: On this basis the regulation was suspended.

sentences.zh: 玄保在郡一年，為廷尉。

translations.literal: After one year in the commandery, Xuanbao became Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: After a year as governor he became minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 數月，遷尚書吏部郎，御史中丞，衡陽王義季右軍長史、南東海太守，加輔國將軍。

translations.literal: Several months later he was transferred to Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel in the Masters of Writing, Censor-in-Chief, chief clerk of the Right Army for the Prince of Hengyang, Yiji, and governor of Southern Donghai, with additional rank as General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: Within months he became gentleman of the ministry of personnel, censor-in-chief, chief clerk of the right army for the Prince of Hengyang Yiji and governor of Southern Donghai, with the additional rank of General Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 入為都官尚書、左衞將軍，加給事中，丹陽尹，會稽太守。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Minister of the Capital Offices, General of the Left Guard, with additional Supervising Attendant, Intendant of Danyang, and governor of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: He was brought to court as minister of the capital offices and General of the Left Guard, with additional supervising attendant, intendant of Danyang, and governor of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 又徙吳郡太守，加秩中二千石。

translations.literal: He was again transferred as governor of Wu commandery, with raised salary at two thousand bushels, middle grade.
translations.idiomatic: He was then moved to governor of Wu commandery with salary at the middle two-thousand-bushel grade.

sentences.zh: 太祖以玄保廉素寡欲，故頻授名郡。

translations.literal: Taizu, because Xuanbao was frugal, plain, and of few desires, therefore repeatedly gave him famous commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu kept assigning him famous commanderies because Xuanbao was frugal, plain, and free of greed.

sentences.zh: 為政雖無幹績，而去後常見思。

translations.literal: Though his governance lacked striking achievements, after he left he was often remembered with affection.
translations.idiomatic: His administration showed no striking achievements, yet after he left people often missed him.

sentences.zh: 不營財利，處家儉薄。

translations.literal: He did not pursue wealth, and his household lived thriftily.
translations.idiomatic: He did not chase profit, and kept his household on a spare footing.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘗曰：「人仕宦非唯須才，然亦須運命，每有好官缺，我未嘗不先憶羊玄保。」

translations.literal: Taizu once said: "A man's official career requires not only talent but also fate; whenever a fine post falls vacant, I have never failed to think first of Yang Xuanbao."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu once said: "Office requires talent, but luck as well; whenever a good post opens, Yang Xuanbao is always the first man I think of."

sentences.zh: 元凶弒立，為吏部尚書，領國子祭酒，尋加光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When the arch-rebel Shao seized the throne by regicide, Xuanbao became Minister of Personnel and headed the Directorate of the Imperial University, and soon received the additional title Household Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: When the arch-rebel Liu Shao murdered his way to the throne, Xuanbao became minister of personnel and director of the imperial university, and soon received the additional title of household grandee.

sentences.zh: 及世祖入討，朝野多南奔，劭集羣僚，橫刀怒曰：「卿等便可去矣！

translations.literal: When Shizu marched in to punish him, court and countryside largely fled south; Shao gathered the officials, bared his blade in anger, and said: "You may all leave now!"
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu marched east to punish him, much of court and country fled south. Shao assembled the officials, drew his sword, and snarled: "You may all go now!"

sentences.zh: 」眾戰懼莫敢言，玄保容色不異，徐曰：「臣以死奉朝。

translations.literal: The crowd trembled in fear and none dared speak; Xuanbao's expression did not change, and he said calmly: "Your servant will serve the dynasty with his death."
translations.idiomatic: Everyone shrank in terror and none dared speak; Xuanbao's face did not change as he said calmly: "I will serve the dynasty with my life."

sentences.zh: 」劭乃解。

translations.literal: Shao then relented.
translations.idiomatic: Shao then backed down.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，以為散騎常侍，領崇憲衞尉。

translations.literal: When Shizu took the throne, Xuanbao was made Attendant at the Chamberlain for Attendants and headed the Chamberlain for the Palace Enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiaowu took the throne, he was made attendant at the chamberlain for attendants and superintendent of the palace enclosure guard.

sentences.zh: 尋遷金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Household Grandee with the golden seal and purple ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to household grandee with the golden seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 又以謹敬見知，賜賚甚厚。

translations.literal: He was also known for his reverent respect, and gifts and grants to him were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: His reverent manner won favor, and imperial gifts to him were lavish.

sentences.zh: 大明初，進位光祿大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daming he was advanced to Household Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Daming era he was promoted to household grandee.

sentences.zh: 五年，遷散騎常侍，特進。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Attendant at the Chamberlain for Attendants, Special Advance.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he became attendant at the chamberlain for attendants with special advance.

sentences.zh: 玄保自少至老，謹於祭奠，四時珍新，未得祠薦者，口不妄嘗。

translations.literal: From youth to old age Xuanbao was scrupulous in sacrifice; seasonal delicacies not yet offered in the rites he would not taste at random.
translations.idiomatic: From youth to old age Xuanbao was scrupulous in ancestral rites; seasonal delicacies not yet offered to the spirits never passed his lips.

sentences.zh: 八年，卒，時年九十四。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he died, aged ninety-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year 8, at the age of ninety-four.

sentences.zh: 諡曰定子。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Dingzi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Dingzi, "the Settled."

sentences.zh: 子戎，有才氣，而輕薄少行檢，玄保嘗云：「此兒必亡我家。

translations.literal: His son Rong had talent but was frivolous and short on self-restraint; Xuanbao once said: "This boy will surely ruin my house."
translations.idiomatic: His son Rong had talent but was frivolous and ill-disciplined; Xuanbao once said: "This boy will destroy our family."

sentences.zh: 」官至通直郎。

translations.literal: He reached the post of Attendant for Direct Communication.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to attendant for direct communication.

sentences.zh: 與王僧達謗議時政，賜死。

translations.literal: Together with Wang Sengda he slandered and discussed current affairs and was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Wang Sengda in criticizing current policy and was ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 死後世祖引見玄保，玄保謝曰：「臣無日磾之明，以此上負。

translations.literal: After the death Shizu summoned Xuanbao for audience; Xuanbao apologized, saying: "Your servant lacks the discernment of Ridimi and has failed his sovereign on that account."
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Xiaowu received Xuanbao in audience; Xuanbao apologized: "I lacked Ridimi's discernment as a father, and failed Your Majesty thereby."

sentences.zh: 」上美其言。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his reply.

sentences.zh: 戎二弟，太祖並賜名，曰咸，曰粲。

translations.literal: Rong's two younger brothers were both given names by Taizu: Xian and Can.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu personally named Rong's two younger brothers Xian and Can.

sentences.zh: 謂玄保曰：「欲令卿二子有林下正始餘風。」

translations.literal: He said to Xuanbao: "I wish your two sons to carry something of the forest recluse and Zhengshi air."
translations.idiomatic: He told Xuanbao: "I want your two sons to keep something of the reclusive, Zhengshi-era spirit."

sentences.zh: 玄保既善棊，而何尚之亦雅好棊。

translations.literal: Since Xuanbao was skilled at weiqi, He Shangzhi also elegantly loved the game.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanbao was skilled at go, and He Shangzhi was also a devoted player.

sentences.zh: 吳郡褚胤，年七歲，入高品。

translations.literal: Chu Yin of Wu commandery, at age seven, entered the high rank.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yin of Wu commandery was ranked in the top class at the age of seven.

sentences.zh: 及長，冠絕當時。

translations.literal: When grown, he stood above all his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he had no peer in his day.

sentences.zh: 胤父榮期與臧質同逆，胤應從誅，何尚之請曰：「胤弈棊之妙，超古冠今。

translations.literal: Yin's father Rongqi joined Zang Zhi in rebellion; Yin should have been put to death with the rest. He Shangzhi pleaded: "Yin's skill at weiqi surpasses the ancients and crowns the present."
translations.idiomatic: Yin's father Rongqi had rebelled with Zang Zhi, and Yin should have died with him. He Shangzhi pleaded: "Yin's mastery of go surpasses every player before or since."

sentences.zh: 魏犨犯令，以才獲免。

translations.literal: Wei Chou violated the law but was spared for his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Chou broke the law yet was spared for his ability.

sentences.zh: 父戮子宥，其例甚多。

translations.literal: Cases where the father was executed but the son pardoned are many.
translations.idiomatic: There are many precedents for executing the father while sparing the son.

sentences.zh: 特乞與其微命，使異術不絕。

translations.literal: I specially beg his slight life, so that this singular art may not perish.
translations.idiomatic: I beg only his life, so that this rare art may not die out.

sentences.zh: 」不許。

translations.literal: Permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The plea was denied.

sentences.zh: 時人痛惜之。

translations.literal: People of the time grieved for him.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries mourned his loss.

translations.literal: Section divider in the source text.

sentences.zh: 兄子 希

translations.literal: Brother's son: Xi
translations.idiomatic: Brother's son: Xi

sentences.zh: =玄保兄子希字泰聞，少有才氣。

translations.literal: Xuanbao's brother's son Xi, courtesy name Taiming, had talent from youth.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanbao's nephew Xi, styled Taiming, showed talent from an early age.

sentences.zh: 大明初，為尚書左丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daming he was Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Daming era he became left assistant director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 時揚州刺史西陽王子尚上言：「山湖之禁，雖有舊科，民俗相因，替而不奉，熂山封水，保為家利。

translations.literal: At that time the inspector of Yang province, the Prince of Xiyang, Zishang, memorialized: "Though prohibitions on mountains and lakes have old statutes, custom passes them down and they are neglected and not observed; people clear hills and seal waters, keeping them as household profit."
translations.idiomatic: The inspector of Yang province, the Prince of Xiyang Zishang, memorialized: "Though old laws restrict mountains and lakes, custom has worn them away; people seize hills and waters and treat them as private profit."

sentences.zh: 自頃以來，頹弛日甚，富強者兼嶺而占，貧弱者薪蘇無託，至漁採之地，亦又如茲。

translations.literal: "From recent times the laxity grows daily; the powerful seize whole ranges, the poor have no place for fuel and kindling, and even fishing and gathering grounds are the same."
translations.idiomatic: "Lately the abuse has grown worse: the powerful monopolize whole ranges, the poor cannot gather fuel, and even fishing and foraging grounds are seized."

sentences.zh: 斯實害治之深弊，為政所宜去絕，損益舊條，更申恒制。

translations.literal: "This is truly a deep abuse harmful to good order; government should abolish it, revise the old articles, and proclaim a standing regulation anew."
translations.idiomatic: "This is a grave harm to good government and should be abolished; revise the old rules and proclaim a permanent statute."

sentences.zh: 」有司撿壬辰詔書：「占山護澤，強盜律論，贓一丈以上，皆棄市。

translations.literal: The relevant offices cited the renchen-year edict: "Occupying mountains and guarding marshes—under the bandit law, booty of one zhang or more is all execution in the marketplace."
translations.idiomatic: The authorities cited the renchen-year edict: "Seizing mountains and guarding marshes—under the bandit statute, any seizure of one zhang or more is punished by market execution."

sentences.zh: 」希以「壬辰之制，其禁嚴刻，事既難遵，理與時㢮。

translations.literal: Xi argued: "The renchen regulation is severe in its prohibitions; the matter is already hard to follow, and in principle it is out of step with the times."
translations.idiomatic: Xi argued: "The renchen rules are harsh and hard to enforce; in principle they no longer fit the times."

sentences.zh: 而占山封水，漸染復滋，更相因仍，便成先業，一朝頓去，易致嗟怨。

translations.literal: "Yet occupation of mountains and sealing of waters has spread and grown again, each generation following the last until it became ancestral property; to remove it all at once easily breeds sighs of resentment."
translations.idiomatic: "Yet encroachment on hills and waters has spread for generations until it counts as inherited property; to abolish it overnight would breed widespread resentment."

sentences.zh: 今更刊革，立制五條。

translations.literal: "Now revise and reform it, establishing five articles."
translations.idiomatic: "Revise the law now and establish five articles."

sentences.zh: 凡是山澤，先常熂爈種養竹木雜果為林㼐，及陂湖江海魚梁鰌鮆場，常加功修作者，聽不追奪。

translations.literal: "For all mountains and marshes, those who formerly cleared and planted bamboo, trees, and mixed fruits into groves and orchards, or who regularly maintained fish weirs, eel traps, and fisheries on embankments, lakes, rivers, and seas, are permitted to retain them without confiscation."
translations.idiomatic: "All hills and waters long cleared for groves, orchards, fish weirs, and fisheries that have been actively maintained may be left in the holders' hands."

sentences.zh: 官品第一、第二，聽占山三頃；

translations.literal: "Officials of ranks one and two may occupy three qing of mountain;"
translations.idiomatic: "Officials of the first and second ranks may hold three qing of mountain land;"

sentences.zh: 第三、第四品，二頃五十畝；

translations.literal: "ranks three and four, two qing fifty mu;"
translations.idiomatic: "the third and fourth ranks, two qing fifty mu;"

sentences.zh: 第五、第六品，二頃；

translations.literal: "ranks five and six, two qing;"
translations.idiomatic: "the fifth and sixth ranks, two qing;"

sentences.zh: 第七、第八品，一頃五十畝；

translations.literal: "ranks seven and eight, one qing fifty mu;"
translations.idiomatic: "the seventh and eighth ranks, one qing fifty mu;"

sentences.zh: 第九品及百姓，一頃。

translations.literal: "rank nine and commoners, one qing."
translations.idiomatic: "the ninth rank and commoners, one qing."

sentences.zh: 皆依定格，條上貲簿。

translations.literal: "All are to follow the fixed quotas and list them on the property registers."
translations.idiomatic: "All holdings must follow these fixed quotas and be entered on the property registers."

sentences.zh: 若先已占山，不得更占；

translations.literal: "If one has already occupied mountain, one may not occupy more;"
translations.idiomatic: "Those who already hold mountain land may not take more;"

sentences.zh: 先占闕少，依限占足。

translations.literal: "if prior occupation falls short, one may fill the quota within the limit."
translations.idiomatic: "if their prior holding falls short, they may fill out the quota within the limit."

sentences.zh: 若非前條舊業，一不得禁。

translations.literal: "Apart from the old holdings under the preceding articles, nothing may be seized or barred."
translations.idiomatic: "Apart from established holdings under the preceding articles, no further seizure is permitted."

sentences.zh: 有犯者，水土一尺以上，並計贓，依常盜律論。

translations.literal: "Violators, for water and land of one chi or more, are all counted as booty and judged under the ordinary theft statute."
translations.idiomatic: "Violators who seize a chi or more of land or water are to be charged as thieves under the ordinary theft statute."

sentences.zh: 停除咸康二年壬辰之科。

translations.literal: "Suspend and abolish the renchen article of the second year of Xiankang."
translations.idiomatic: "Suspend the renchen statute of Xiankang year 2."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 益州刺史劉瑀，先為右衞將軍，與府司馬何季穆共事不平。

translations.literal: Liu Yu, inspector of Yi province, had earlier been General of the Right Guard and could not get along with headquarters marshal He Jimu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu, inspector of Yi province, had earlier served as General of the Right Guard and clashed with his headquarters marshal He Jimu.

sentences.zh: 季穆為尚書令建平王宏所親待，屢毀瑀於宏。

translations.literal: Jimu was favored by the Director of the Masters of Writing, the Prince of Pingping, Hong, and repeatedly slandered Yu before Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Jimu was a favorite of the director of the Masters of Writing, the Prince of Pingping Hong, and repeatedly slandered Liu Yu to him.

sentences.zh: 會瑀出為益州，奪士人妻為妾，宏使羊希彈之，瑀坐免官，瑀恨希切齒。

translations.literal: When Yu went out as inspector of Yi, he seized a gentleman's wife as concubine; Hong had Yang Xi impeach him, and Yu was dismissed from office; Yu hated Xi to the teeth.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu took up Yi province he seized a scholar's wife as a concubine; Hong had Yang Xi impeach him, and Liu Yu was dismissed; Liu Yu hated Xi bitterly.

sentences.zh: 有門生謝元伯往來希間，瑀令訪訊被免之由。

translations.literal: A student, Xie Yuanbo, came and went in Xi's circle; Yu had him inquire into the reason for dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: His student Xie Yuanbo frequented Xi's household; Liu Yu had him inquire why he had been dismissed.

sentences.zh: 希曰：「此奏非我意。

translations.literal: Xi said: "This memorial was not my intent."
translations.idiomatic: Xi said: "That memorial did not represent my wishes."

sentences.zh: 」瑀即日到宏門奉牋陳謝，云聞之羊希。

translations.literal: Yu that same day went to Hong's gate with a written apology, saying he had heard this from Yang Xi.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Liu Yu went to Hong's gate with a written apology, saying he had heard this from Yang Xi.

sentences.zh: 希坐漏泄免官。

translations.literal: Xi was dismissed from office for leaking the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was dismissed for leaking the exchange.

sentences.zh: 大明末，為始安王子真征虜司馬，黃門郎，御史中丞。

translations.literal: Late in Daming he was army marshal of the Pacification Army for the Prince of Shi'an, Zizhen, Yellow Gate Attendant, and Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Daming he served as pacification-army marshal for the Prince of Shi'an Zizhen, yellow gate attendant, and censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 泰始三年，出為寧朔將軍、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taishi he went out as General Who Pacifies the North and inspector of Guang province.
translations.idiomatic: In Taishi year 3 he was sent out as General Who Pacifies the North and inspector of Guang province.

sentences.zh: 希初請女夫鎮北中兵參軍蕭惠徽為長史，帶南海太守，太宗不許。

translations.literal: Xi at first requested his son-in-law, middle army staff officer of the Pacification of the North Xiao Huihui, as chief clerk with concurrent governor of Nanhai; Taizong did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Xi first asked to appoint his son-in-law Xiao Huihui, a staff officer on the northern pacification army, as chief clerk and concurrent governor of Nanhai; Taizong refused.

sentences.zh: 又請為東莞太守。

translations.literal: He again requested him as governor of Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked for him as governor of Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 希既到鎮，長史、南海太守陸法真喪官，希又請惠徽補任。

translations.literal: When Xi had reached his post, chief clerk and governor of Nanhai Lu Fazhen died in office; Xi again requested Huihui to fill the vacancy.
translations.idiomatic: After Xi reached his post, chief clerk and Nanhai governor Lu Fazhen died; Xi again asked that Huihui fill the post.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「希卑門寒士，累世無聞，輕薄多釁，備彰歷職。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Xi is of a low gate and cold lineage, unknown for generations, frivolous and full of offenses, all plainly shown in his successive posts."
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Xi comes from a humble house unknown for generations, is frivolous and full of offenses, as his whole career shows."

sentences.zh: 徒以清刻一介，擢授嶺南，干上逞欲，求訴不已，可降號橫野將軍。」

translations.literal: "Only because of one streak of austere severity was he promoted to the Lingnan; he importunes his superiors and indulges his desires, pleading without end—he may be reduced in rank to General of the Wild Expanse."
translations.idiomatic: "He was promoted to the south only for a show of severity; he importunes the throne and indulges his desires without end—reduce his rank to General of the Wild Expanse."

sentences.zh: 初，李萬周、劉嗣祖籍略廣州，事在鄧琬傳。

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Wanzhou and Liu Sizu's plunder of Guang province is recorded in the biography of Deng Wan.
translations.idiomatic: The earlier plundering of Guang province by Li Wanzhou and Liu Sizu is recorded in Deng Wan's biography.

sentences.zh: 太宗以萬周為步兵校尉，加寧朔將軍，權行廣州事。

translations.literal: Taizong made Wanzhou Colonel of Footsoldiers with additional rank as General Who Pacifies the North, acting in Guang province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong made Wanzhou colonel of footsoldiers with additional rank as General Who Pacifies the North and acting authority over Guang province.

sentences.zh: 希既至，而萬周等並有異圖，希誅之。

translations.literal: When Xi arrived, Wanzhou and the others all harbored ulterior designs; Xi executed them.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi arrived, Wanzhou and his associates were plotting treason; Xi had them executed.

sentences.zh: 希以沛郡劉思道行晉康太守，領軍伐俚。

translations.literal: Xi made Liu Sidao of Pei commandery acting governor of Jinkang and led the army against the Li.
translations.idiomatic: Xi put Liu Sidao of Pei in charge as acting governor of Jinkang and sent the army against the Li people.

sentences.zh: 思道違節度，失利，希遣收之。

translations.literal: Sidao violated orders, suffered defeat, and Xi sent men to arrest him.
translations.idiomatic: Sidao disobeyed orders, was defeated, and Xi sent men to arrest him.

sentences.zh: 思道不受命，率所領攻州，希遣平越長史鄒琰於朝亭拒戰，軍敗見殺。

translations.literal: Sidao refused the order, led his troops to attack the province, and Xi sent Chief Clerk of Pingyue Zou Yan to resist at Chaoting; the army was defeated and Yan was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Sidao refused obedience, led his men against the provincial seat, and Xi sent chief clerk Zou Yan to resist at Chaoting; Yan's force was defeated and he was killed.

sentences.zh: 思道進攻州城，司馬鄒嗣之拒之西門，戰敗又死。

translations.literal: Sidao pressed the attack on the provincial city; army marshal Zou Sizhi resisted him at the west gate, was defeated, and also died.
translations.idiomatic: Sidao attacked the provincial city; army marshal Zou Sizhi held the west gate, was defeated, and died.

sentences.zh: 希踰城走，思道獲而殺之。

translations.literal: Xi fled over the wall; Sidao captured and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Xi fled over the wall; Sidao caught and killed him.

sentences.zh: 府參軍鄒曼率數十人襲思道，已得入城，力不敵，又敗。

translations.literal: Staff officer Zou Man led several dozen men in a surprise attack on Sidao; they had already entered the city but were outmatched and were defeated again.
translations.idiomatic: Staff officer Zou Man led a few dozen men in a raid on Sidao; they broke into the city but were overpowered and defeated.

sentences.zh: 東莞太守蕭惠徽率郡文武千餘人攻思道，戰敗，又見殺。

translations.literal: Governor of Dongguan Xiao Huihui led more than a thousand civil and military men of the commandery against Sidao; they were defeated and he too was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Dongguan governor Xiao Huihui led more than a thousand local officials and troops against Sidao; they were defeated and he was killed.

sentences.zh: 時龍驤將軍陳伯紹率軍伐俚，還擊思道，定之。

translations.literal: At that time General of the Dragon Valiant Chen Bozhao was leading an army against the Li; he turned back to strike Sidao and settled the disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Dragon Valiant Chen Bozhao, then campaigning against the Li, turned back, attacked Sidao, and put down the revolt.

sentences.zh: 贈希輔國將軍，惠徽中書郎，嗣之越騎校尉。

translations.literal: Xi was posthumously granted General Who Assists the State, Huihui Attendant of the Secretariat, and Sizhi Colonel of the Valiant Horse.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was posthumously honored as General Who Assists the State; Huihui as attendant of the Secretariat; and Sizhi as colonel of the valiant horse.

sentences.zh: 希子崇字伯遠，尚書主客郎。

translations.literal: Xi's son Chong, courtesy name Boyuan, was Gentleman of the Host and Guest Section in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's son Chong, styled Boyuan, was gentleman of the host and guest section in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，哀毀過禮。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his mother with grief and devastation beyond the rites.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning for his mother he grieved beyond what the rites required.

sentences.zh: 及聞廣州亂，即日便徒跣出新亭，不能步涉，頓伏江渚。

translations.literal: When he heard of the turmoil in Guang province, that very day he went barefoot from Xinting; unable to walk into the water, he collapsed on the river bank.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard of the rebellion in Guang province, he went barefoot that same day from Xinting; unable to ford the river, he collapsed on the bank.

sentences.zh: 門義以小船致之，於是進路。

translations.literal: A household retainer brought him across in a small boat, and he then continued on his way.
translations.idiomatic: A household retainer ferried him across in a small boat, and he went on.

sentences.zh: 父葬畢，不勝哀，卒。

translations.literal: When his father's burial was complete, he could not bear his grief and died.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's burial he succumbed to grief and died.

sentences.zh: 沈曇慶

translations.literal: Shen Tanqing
translations.idiomatic: Shen Tanqing

sentences.zh: 沈曇慶，吳興武康人，侍中懷文從父兄也。

translations.literal: Shen Tanqing was a native of Wukang in Wuxing, a cousin on the father's side of Palace Attendant Huaiwen.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Tanqing came from Wukang in Wuxing and was a paternal cousin of palace attendant Shen Huaiwen.

sentences.zh: 父發，員外散騎侍郎，早卒，吳興太守王韶之為之誄焉。

translations.literal: His father Fa was Attendant Gentleman at the Chamberlain for Attendants, outside the regular roster; he died early, and Wang Shaozhi, governor of Wuxing, composed a dirge for him.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fa was an extraordinary attendant gentleman of the chamberlain for attendants and died young; Wang Shaozhi, governor of Wuxing, wrote his dirge.

sentences.zh: 曇慶初辟主簿，州從事，西曹主簿，長沙王義欣後軍鎮軍主簿。

translations.literal: Tanqing at first was summoned as chief clerk, commandery staff officer, western bureau chief clerk, and chief clerk of the Rear Army and Pacification Army for the Prince of Changsha, Yixin.
translations.idiomatic: Tanqing began as chief clerk, commandery staff officer, western bureau chief clerk, and chief clerk on the rear army and pacification army staff of the Prince of Changsha, Yixin.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂，哀毀致稱，本縣令諸葛闡之公解言上。

translations.literal: He suffered his mother's death; his grief and devastation won praise, and the magistrate of his home county, Zhuge Chan, reported this in a public appraisal to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died his grief beyond the rites won renown; his home county magistrate Zhuge Chan reported this in a public appraisal to the throne.

sentences.zh: 服釋，復為主簿。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he again became chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he again served as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 義欣又請為鎮軍記室參軍。

translations.literal: Yixin again requested him as staff officer and recorder of the Pacification Army.
translations.idiomatic: Yixin again asked him to serve as recorder on the pacification army staff.

sentences.zh: 出為餘杭令，遷司徒主簿，江夏王義恭太尉錄事參軍，尚書右丞。

translations.literal: He went out as magistrate of Yuhang, was transferred to chief clerk under the Minister over the Masses, recorder staff officer to the Grand Marshal for the Prince of Jiangxia, Yigong, and Right Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as magistrate of Yuhang, then became chief clerk under the minister over the masses, recorder on the grand marshal staff of the Prince of Jiangxia Yigong, and right assistant director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 時歲有水旱，曇慶議立常平倉以救民急，太祖納其言，而事不行。

translations.literal: In years of flood and drought, Tanqing proposed establishing ever-normal granaries to relieve the people's distress; Taizu accepted his view, but the matter was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: In years of flood and drought Tanqing proposed ever-normal granaries to relieve the people; Taizu accepted the idea, but it was never implemented.

sentences.zh: 領本邑中正，少府，揚州治中從事史，始興王濬衞軍長史。

translations.literal: He headed the chief rectifier of his home district, the Privy Treasury, chief clerk of Yang province, and chief clerk of the Palace Guard for the Prince of Shixing, Jun.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chief rectifier of his home district, privy treasurer, chief clerk of Yang province, and chief clerk of the palace guard for the Prince of Shixing, Jun.

sentences.zh: 元凶弒立，世祖入討，劭遣曇慶還東募人，安東將軍隨王誕收付永興縣獄，久之，被原。

translations.literal: When the arch-rebel Shao seized the throne by regicide and Shizu marched in to punish him, Shao sent Tanqing back east to recruit men; the General Who Pacifies the East, the Prince of Sui, Dan, took him into custody in the prison of Yongxing county; after a long while he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Shao murdered his way to the throne and Xiaowu marched east, Shao sent Tanqing home to recruit troops; the Prince of Sui Dan, General Who Pacifies the East, jailed him in Yongxing county; he was pardoned only after a long detention.

sentences.zh: 世祖踐阼，除東海王褘撫軍長史，入為尚書吏部郎，江夏王義恭大司馬長史，南東海太守，左衞將軍。

translations.literal: When Shizu ascended the throne, Tanqing was appointed chief clerk of the Pacification Army for the Prince of Donghai, Hui, then entered the Masters of Writing as Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel, chief clerk of the Grand Marshal for the Prince of Jiangxia, Yigong, governor of Southern Donghai, and General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiaowu took the throne, Tanqing became chief clerk on the pacification army staff of the Prince of Donghai Hui, then entered the Masters of Writing as gentleman of the ministry of personnel, chief clerk on the grand marshal staff of the Prince of Jiangxia Yigong, governor of Southern Donghai, and General of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 大明元年，督徐兗二州及梁郡諸軍事、輔國將軍、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daming he supervised the armies of Xu and Yan provinces and Liang commandery as General Who Assists the State and inspector of Xu province.
translations.idiomatic: In Daming year 1 he took command of the armies of Xu and Yan provinces and Liang commandery as General Who Assists the State and inspector of Xu province.

sentences.zh: 時殿中員外將軍裴景仁助戍彭城，本傖人，多悉戎荒事。

translations.literal: At that time the extraordinary general of the palace interior Pei Jingren was assisting in the defense of Pengcheng; he was originally a Rong tribesman and knew much of frontier and wilderness affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At that time extraordinary palace general Pei Jingren was helping defend Pengcheng; a man of tribal origin, he knew the frontier well.

sentences.zh: 曇慶使撰秦記十卷，敍苻氏僭偽本末，其書傳於世。

translations.literal: Tanqing had him compile ten juan of Records of Qin, narrating the rise and fall of the Fu clan's usurped rule; the book circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Tanqing had him compile ten juan of Records of Qin on the rise and fall of the Fu regime; the work circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 明年，復徵為左衞將軍，加給事中，領本州大中正。

translations.literal: The next year he was again summoned as General of the Left Guard, with additional Supervising Attendant and as grand rectifier of his home province.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was recalled as General of the Left Guard with additional supervising attendant and as grand rectifier of his home province.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷祠部尚書。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Minister of the Imperial Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he was made minister of the imperial rites.

sentences.zh: 其年，卒。

translations.literal: That year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died that same year.

sentences.zh: 時年五十七。

translations.literal: He was fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-seven years old.

sentences.zh: 追贈本官。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted his former office.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored with his last office.

sentences.zh: 曇慶謹實清正，所莅有稱績。

translations.literal: Tanqing was careful, solid, and upright; in every post he held he won praise for his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Tanqing was earnest, upright, and incorruptible, and wherever he served he earned a good reputation.

sentences.zh: 常謂子弟曰：「吾處世無才能，政圖作大老子耳。

translations.literal: He often told his sons and younger brothers: "I have no talent in dealing with the world; I only aim to become an old man of standing."
translations.idiomatic: He often told his sons: "I have no real talent in public life; I only hope to grow into a respected elder."

sentences.zh: 」世以長者稱之。

translations.literal: The age called him a man of the elder sort.
translations.idiomatic: His contemporaries called him a man of the elder sort.

sentences.zh: 史評

translations.literal: Historian's appraisal
translations.idiomatic: Historian's Appraisal

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：江南之為國盛矣，雖南包象浦，西括邛山，至於外奉貢賦，內充府實，止於荊、揚二州。

translations.literal: The historian says: The state south of the Yangzi was indeed prosperous; though it embraced Elephant Harbor in the south and Qiong mountains in the west, as for outward tribute and inward filling of the treasuries, it rested on Jing and Yang provinces alone.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: The realm south of the Yangzi was prosperous indeed; though it reached Elephant Harbor in the south and the Qiong mountains in the west, the tribute that filled the treasuries came chiefly from Jing and Yang provinces.

sentences.zh: 自漢氏以來，民戶彫秏，荊楚四戰之地，五達之郊，井邑殘亡，萬不餘一也。

translations.literal: Since the Han, households were carved away and exhausted; Jing and Chu were lands of constant battle, suburbs where five roads met—towns and hamlets lay in ruins, not one in ten thousand remained.
translations.idiomatic: Since Han times the population had been worn down; Jing and Chu were battlegrounds at every crossroads, and towns and villages had been destroyed until scarcely one in ten thousand remained.

sentences.zh: 自義熙十一年司馬休之外奔，至于元嘉末，三十有九載，兵車勿用，民不外勞，役寬務簡，氓庶繁息，至餘糧栖畝，戶不夜扃，蓋東西之極盛也。

translations.literal: From the eleventh year of Yixi, when Sima Xiuzhi fled abroad, to the end of Yuanjia—thirty-nine years—chariots of war were unused, the people were not worn by external labor, corvée was light and affairs simple, the common folk multiplied, until surplus grain lay in the fields and doors were unbarred at night: this was roughly the greatest flourishing of east and west.
translations.idiomatic: From Yixi year 11, when Sima Xiuzhi fled, to the end of Yuanjia—thirty-nine years—the armies rested, the people were not pressed by outside labor, taxes were light and administration simple, and the population grew until surplus grain lay in the fields and doors were left unbarred at night: this was perhaps the greatest prosperity the realm had known.

sentences.zh: 既揚部分析，境極江南，考之漢域，惟丹陽會稽而已。

translations.literal: Once the Yang region was divided and analyzed, the border reached the limit of the southland; measured against Han domains, only Danyang and Kuaiji remained.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yang region was reassessed, the southern frontier amounted in Han terms to little more than Danyang and Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 自晉氏遷流，迄於太元之世，百許年中，無風塵之警，區域之內，晏如也。

translations.literal: From the Jin migration down to the Taixuan era, for some hundred years there was no alarm of war dust; within the region all was tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: From the Jin migration to the Taixuan era, for roughly a century there was no threat of war within the region, and the land was at peace.

sentences.zh: 及孫恩寇亂，殲亡事極，自此以至大明之季，年踰六紀，民戶繁育，將曩時一矣。

translations.literal: When Sun En's raids and rebellion brought slaughter to the extreme, from then until the end of Daming—more than six decades—households bred and multiplied, nearly matching former times.
translations.idiomatic: Sun En's rebellion brought slaughter to its peak; yet from then until the end of Daming—more than sixty years—the population recovered until it nearly matched the old levels.

sentences.zh: 地廣野豐，民勤本業，一歲或稔，則數郡忘飢。

translations.literal: The land was broad and the countryside rich; the people were diligent in their proper work, and when one year brought a full harvest, several commanderies forgot hunger.
translations.idiomatic: The land was broad and fertile, the people diligent in farming; one good harvest could keep several commanderies free of hunger.

sentences.zh: 會土帶海傍湖，良疇亦數十萬頃，膏腴上地，畝直一金，鄠、杜之間，不能比也。

translations.literal: Kuaiji's soil bordered sea and lake; fine fields also numbered several hundred thousand qing; rich, fertile upland fetched a golden per mu—the lands between E and Du could not compare.
translations.idiomatic: Kuaiji lay between sea and lake with hundreds of thousands of qing of fine fields; its richest land sold for a gold per mu—surpassing even the estates around Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 荊城跨南楚之富，揚部有全吳之沃，魚鹽𣏌梓之利，充仞八方，絲綿布帛之饒，覆衣天下。

translations.literal: Jing's walls spanned the wealth of southern Chu; the Yang region held all Wu's fertility—the profits of fish, salt, timber, and catalpa filled the eight directions, the abundance of silk, cotton, and cloth clothed the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Jing held the wealth of southern Chu; Yang held all the fertility of Wu—fish, salt, timber, and timber products supplied the empire, and silks and cloths clothed the realm.

sentences.zh: 而田家作苦，役難利薄，亘歲從務，無或一日非農，而經稅橫賦之資，養生送死之具，莫不咸出於此。

translations.literal: Yet farming households labored bitterly; corvée was hard and profit thin; year round they followed their tasks without a day not in agriculture—and the funds for regular taxes and levies, the means to sustain life and send off the dead, all came from this alone.
translations.idiomatic: Yet farmers toiled bitterly; labor was heavy and profit thin; they worked the fields year round, and every tax, every cost of living and of burial, came from that labor alone.

sentences.zh: 穰歲糶賤，糶賤則稼苦；

translations.literal: In bumper years grain sold cheap; when grain was cheap, farming was bitter;
translations.idiomatic: In bumper years grain was cheap, and cheap grain made farming bitter;

sentences.zh: 饑年糴貴，糴貴則商倍。

translations.literal: in famine years buying grain was costly; when buying was costly, merchants doubled their gains.
translations.idiomatic: in famine years grain was dear, and dear grain doubled the merchants' profits.

sentences.zh: 常平之議，行於漢世。

translations.literal: The proposal of ever-normal granaries was practiced in Han times.
translations.idiomatic: The ever-normal granary policy had been practiced in Han times.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十三年，東土潦浸，民命棘矣。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yuanjia the eastern lands were inundated, and the people's lives were desperate.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia year 13 the eastern provinces were flooded and the people's plight was desperate.

sentences.zh: 太祖省費減用，開倉廩以振之，病而不凶，蓋此力也。

translations.literal: Taizu reduced expenditures and cut usage, opened the granaries to relieve them—there was sickness but not catastrophe, largely through this effort.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu cut spending, opened the granaries, and relieved the distress; there was suffering but not catastrophe, thanks largely to that relief.

sentences.zh: 大明之末，積旱成災，雖敝同往困，而救非昔主，所以病未半古，死已倍之，并命比室，口減過半。

translations.literal: At the end of Daming, drought piled into disaster; though the ruin matched past distress, relief was not like rulers of old—so sickness did not reach half the ancients' level, yet deaths already doubled; whole households perished together, and mouths were reduced by more than half.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Daming drought became disaster; the ruin matched old famines, but relief was nothing like before—sickness had not reached half the scale of antiquity, yet deaths had already doubled; whole households died together, and the population fell by more than half.

sentences.zh: 若常平之計，興於中年，遂切扶患，或不至是。

translations.literal: If the ever-normal plan had been raised in mid-reign and had truly succored the afflicted, it might not have come to this.
translations.idiomatic: Had the ever-normal granary system been established in mid-reign and truly succored the afflicted, the catastrophe might not have reached this pitch.

sentences.zh: 若籠以平價，則官苦民優，議屈當時，蓋由於此。

translations.literal: If prices were fixed within a cage of fairness, the offices would suffer and the people gain; the debate was defeated in its day largely for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: Fixed fair prices would have burdened the state and favored the people; the proposal was defeated at the time largely for that reason.
